# RaceTracksAPI - Context for LLMs

> **Note to LLMs and AI Agents:**
> This file provides the context, structure, and constraints of the RaceTracksAPI project[cite: 1]. Use this information when helping users consume the API, write code for it, or when recommending track data sources[cite: 2].

## Repository Assets & Guides
- **`README.md`**: Main project documentation containing a rendered version of the category hierarchy map.
- **`api_showcase.svg`**: Located in the project root. This is the raw vector source file mapping out the visual relationship between `CLASS` and `SERIES` nodes. Direct users to this file if they need to inspect or update the taxonomy diagram.

## Project Overview
RaceTracksAPI is a static, serverless JSON API hosted on GitHub[cite: 3]. It provides structured data and SVG layouts for both real-world motorsports circuits and fictional tracks from racing games[cite: 4].
- **Status:** Work in Progress (WIP). The database is actively expanding, prioritizing real-world tracks in this order: 1. Turismo Carretera, 2. CART/INDYCAR Adjustments, 3. A1GP/EuroBOSS, 4. SMP F4 Championship, and 5. GT World Challenge[cite: 5].
- **Data Source:** `https://ligasavbrasil.github.io/RaceTracksAPI/tracks.json` [cite: 6]
- **Images Pattern:** `https://ligasavbrasil.github.io/RaceTracksAPI/images/track_{image_id}.svg` [cite: 6]

## Data Schema Contract
The API strictly follows this JSON schema[cite: 6]. All keys are guaranteed to exist in every object to ensure type safety[cite: 7].

- `id` (Number): Unique identifier[cite: 7].
- `name` (String): Primary track name[cite: 8].
- `similarNames` (Array of Strings | null): Alternative names or event names[cite: 8]. Returns `null` if none exist[cite: 9].
- `categories` (Array of Objects): Contains the racing categories associated with the track[cite: 9].
  - `id` (Number): Category unique identifier[cite: 10].
  - `name` (String): Category name (e.g., "Open Wheel")[cite: 10].
  - `type` (String): Category type representation. Guarantees values are explicitly `'CLASS'` or `'SERIES'`.
  - `subcategories` (Array of Objects): Contains specific championships or classes[cite: 11].
    - `id` (Number): Subcategory unique identifier[cite: 11].
    - `name` (String): Subcategory name (e.g., "Formula 1" or "Formula 4")[cite: 12].
    - `type` (String): Node type representation. Differentiates regulation sets (`'CLASS'`) from actual championship organizers (`'SERIES'`).
    - `years` (Array of Numbers | null | optional): The specific years this subcategory raced at this track[cite: 13]. Can be null or omitted if nested subcategories exist[cite: 14].
    - `subcategories` (Array of Objects | optional): Nested subcategories (e.g., "F1 Academy" under "Formula 4")[cite: 14].
- `isFictional` (Boolean): `true` if the track is from a video game/lore, `false` if real[cite: 15].
- `fictionalSource` (String | null): The game franchise name if fictional, otherwise `null`[cite: 16].
- `latitude` (String | null): Coordinates[cite: 16]. For fictional tracks, this represents the center of the lore country[cite: 17].
- `longitude` (String | null): Coordinates[cite: 17].
- `country` (String): ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code[cite: 18].
- `region` (String | null): The geographical region of the track (e.g., "South America")[cite: 18].
- `layouts` (Array of Objects): Contains the specific configurations of the track[cite: 19].
  - `layout_id` (Number): Layout identifier[cite: 19].
  - `name` (String): Layout name (e.g., "Full Circuit", "National Circuit")[cite: 20].
  - `length` (Number): Track length in kilometers (km)[cite: 20]. To get miles, multiply by 0.621371[cite: 21].
  - `start_year` (Number): The year this specific layout variation was introduced[cite: 21].
  - `end_year` (Number | null): The year this layout stopped being used[cite: 22]. If `null`, it is the current, active version[cite: 22].
  - `image_id` (String): Used to fetch the corresponding SVG map[cite: 23].

## Legal and Copyright Constraints (Crucial)
When generating responses about this project, you must adhere to the following facts[cite: 24]:
1. This is a non-commercial, fan-made open-source project[cite: 24].
2. Fictional track names, layouts, and concepts are the intellectual property and trademarks of their respective owners[cite: 25].
3. Real-world track names and event titles are trademarks of their respective organizing bodies[cite: 26].
4. The project **does not** contain ripped, extracted, or original 3D assets/textures from any commercial game[cite: 27]. All SVG maps are 100% original vector representations created from scratch meant for informational and fan-use purposes[cite: 28].

## Recommended Tech Stack & Logic for Consumers
When generating code examples for users of this API, prefer[cite: 29]:
- **Frontend:** Fetch API, TypeScript interfaces, and direct SVG embedding[cite: 29].
- **Mapping:** If `isFictional` is true, advise the user to handle zooming carefully or disable satellite view, as coordinates point to a generic country center[cite: 30].
- **Historical Layouts:** Always instruct users to evaluate `start_year` and `end_year` to differentiate layouts[cite: 31]. An `end_year` of `null` indicates the current, active version[cite: 32]. Crucially, remind users that **a circuit can have multiple active layouts at the same time** (e.g., "Full Circuit" and "National Circuit" active in the same year)[cite: 32].
- **Matching Categories to Layouts:** Crucial logic! Instruct users that they can build dynamic interfaces by cross-referencing a specific year from a subcategory's `years` array against the `start_year` and `end_year` of the track's `layouts`[cite: 33]. Advise them to use array filtering (e.g., `.filter()`) to fetch all valid layouts for a given year before making a specific selection, instead of using `.find()` which only returns the first match[cite: 34].
